subject: trying to plot a linear extrapolation with error limits

messages.author: b2b3ce36517d67c5
messages.subject: trying to plot a linear extrapolation with error limits
parts:
I have a plot *almost* like I want it, but not quite. I want to show
the actual data, and then where the data ends, a linear extrapolation
with an error cone extending away from the current data range. The
problem I am having is getting the extrapolated lines to stop at the
data. The current plot is at http://www.ajackson.org/BugList.png .

The plotting bits I have right now look like this (a bit of a mess) :

p <- qplot(Date, Bugs, data=data, geom=c('smooth','point'),
ylim=c(0,150), main="Bugs Waiting to be Fixed")
p = p + stat_smooth(method="lm", se=FALSE, colour="red")
p = p + scale_x_date(lim = c(as.Date("2011-01-18"),
as.Date("2011-02-25")))
p = p + geom_abline(intercept=coef(fit)[1], slope=coef(fit)[2],
x=extrap, linetype=3)
p = p + geom_abline(intercept=coef(minfit)[1], slope=coef(minfit)[2],
x=extrap, linetype=2)
p = p + geom_abline(intercept=coef(maxfit)[1], slope=coef(maxfit)[2],
x=extrap, linetype=2)

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: trying to plot a linear extrapolation with error limits
parts:
I'm not entirely sure I understand the problem and you've not supplied any data to play with, but hopefully I can be of some help. 

If I understand the problem right. You have data that appears to stop around January 26/27, but your lines are plotted all the way out to Feb 25. You want the extrapolated lines to stop where you have data. 

I've not used as.Date() all that much but it seems to me that the problem is with this line of code:
p = p + scale_x_date(lim = c(as.Date("2011-01-18"), as.Date("2011-02-25")))

You're telling ggplot to plot everything out until the 25th and it is doing so. If you want it to only plot the extrapolated lines to... say a few days beyond your data you should calculate the maximum day in your data and add a few days. Something like max(data$Date)+3. I'm not sure if you can just add three to a date, but I'm sure there's something out there. 

Is that what you're after? 

If not, could you clarify your problem and provide a reproducible example with example data? 

Brandon

(days[length(days)]-days[1])
maxdays = days - deltay/(m+stderr_slope)*(days-days[1])/
(days[length(days)]-days[1])
bugs = coef(fit)[2]*days + coef(fit)[1]

maxpredict = data.frame(bugs, maxdays)

minfit = lm(bugs ~ mindays, data = minpredict)
maxfit = lm(bugs ~ maxdays, data = maxpredict)

p <- qplot(Date, Bugs, data=data, geom=c('smooth','point'),
ylim=c(0,150), main="Bugs Waiting to be Fixed")
p = p + stat_smooth(method="lm", se=FALSE, colour="red")

x=extrap, linetype=2)

p + geom_abline(intercept=coef(maxfit)[1], slope=coef(maxfit)[2],
x=extrap, linetype=2)

Unless there is a x_limit attribute for geom_abline() that I'm unaware of, it seems like you'll have to use geom_segment... See here.

Unless I'm not understanding still, which is entirely a possibility. It is a weekend after all. 

B

messages.subject: Re: trying to plot a linear extrapolation with error limits
parts:
I got it. What I needed to use was geom_line, but I also needed to
build data frames for each line and call it like :

p = p + geom_line(data=minpredict, aes(x=mindays, y=bugs, linetype=2))
p = p + geom_line(data=avgpredict, aes(x=avgdays, y=bugs, linetype=3))
p + geom_line(data=maxpredict, aes(x=maxdays, y=bugs, linetype=2))


Thanks!
